Subject: Security annex and subprocessor onboarding for DPA

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Legal and security here at FinBank reviewed the DPA draft and we'd like to discuss three items before execution:

- Stronger text in the TOMs exhibit around encryption at rest (HSM-backed keys) and key separation (per-customer keys).
- The subprocessor onboarding and approval process — we need visibility into new subprocessor additions and an escalation window for objections.
- Data transfer mechanisms: please confirm whether Redwood will rely on SCCs, the Data Privacy Framework, or offer EU data residency options.

Also, given our timelines, we'd prefer to complete redline review and eSign by mid-December. Can you:
1) confirm whether you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM?
2) share your current subprocessor inventory and cadence for updates?
3) indicate preferred eSign provider (DocuSign or AdobeSign) and whether you can lock the TOMs exhibit in the DPA rather than a separate annex?

If easier, we can do a 30-minute call this week — security + legal will join.

Regards,
Amir Qureshi
Head of Security, FinBank

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Date: 2026-12-02T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Security annex and subprocessor onboarding for DPA

Amir — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: yes to BYOK (customer-managed keys) with HSM-backed KMS; yes to an objection window for new subprocessors; and we support both DocuSign and AdobeSign for execution.

I've attached a proposed Security Annex (Redwood_DPA_SecurityAnnex_v2.docx) and an updated TOMs exhibit (Redwood_TOMs_Exhibit_v2.pdf) with redlines showing:
- Per-customer keys and key separation language (we create distinct key namespaces per customer).
- HSM-backed key material for hosted KMS; support for customer-provided keys via external HSM import or AWS KMS Customer Key (we describe the integration options in the annex).
- Key rotation cadence and audit logging requirements (keeps rotation default 90 days; can be altered by contract).

Subprocessor inventory is included as a CSV attachment; we publish an updated list within 5 business days of changes and provide a 10-business-day objection window for new subprocessors that process EU personal data.

Regarding data transfers: we currently rely on SCCs and also offer EU-region hosting where data can remain in-region. We are tracking DPFramework developments but will not rely on it as the sole mechanism unless requested.

Proposed next steps:
1) Legal review of the annex and TOMs redlines (attached).
2) If acceptable, sign via DocuSign/AdobeSign — we can issue an envelope that locks Exhibit B (TOMs).
3) If any specific KMS ceremony or attestation is required, we can route to our Crypto/Ops team for a short technical addendum.

Available for a call tomorrow 10–11am PT if you'd like to go through the redlines.

Thanks,

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Voss <elena.voss@finbank.com>

Date: 2026-12-08T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Security annex - FinBank redlines (TOMs focus)

Dylan / Monica — attaching FinBank legal redlines. Key asks from our side (summarized):

- KMS/key escrow: We need clarity on whether Redwood will retain any capability to reconstruct customer keys (we prefer negative confirmation — no escrow unless explicitly agreed for regulated lines).
- Key rotation & notification: we want mandatory 60-day rotation for keys that protect regulated data and a 30-day notice if Redwood plans to change rotation defaults.
- Subprocessor approval: we require a 15-business-day objection window for critical subprocessors, monthly notification for routine additions, and the right to request a security assessment for high-risk subprocessors.
- Audit rights: FinBank requires the ability to schedule an annual SOC2+ attestation review or accept recent third-party audit reports; we need an explicit clause.

We also have a couple of edits to the TOMs exhibit around encryption algorithms and backup key handling. Please provide an updated TOMs PDF with our edits incorporated and confirm DocuSign is fine for signature.

Attaching: FinBank_DPA_Redlines_2026-12-08.pdf

Thanks,
Elena Voss
Senior Counsel — Privacy & Data Governance, FinBank
elena.voss@finbank.com
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Elena Voss <elena.voss@finbank.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-15T10:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Security annex - FinBank redlines (TOMs focus)

Elena — thanks for the thorough redlines. We pushed back on a few items and incorporated the rest in the updated TOMs exhibit attached (Redwood_TOMs_Exhibit_v2.pdf). Highlights of our positions and edits:

1) Key escrow: Redwood's standard position is that we do NOT retain key escrow capability. We offer two supported models: 
   - Managed KMS (Redwood-managed HSM): keys are generated and stored in HSM with access controls; Redwood operators do not have plaintext access.
   - BYOK (customer-supplied KMS/HSM): customer retains key ownership and control; Redwood never has access to plaintext.
We will not include a general key-escrow clause. If FinBank requires escrow for specific regulated assets, we can scope that as a separate, negotiated addendum.

2) Key rotation: we accepted a compromise: default rotation schedule will be 90 days but for regulated data classes we will include optional 60-day rotation in the contract exhibit if the customer elects that class. We added a 30-day notice for planned changes to defaults.

3) Subprocessor objection window: we can support a 15-business-day objection window for critical subprocessors that process regulated data. For routine subprocessors, we will publish monthly updates and provide a 10-business-day notification window. We added language for a security assessment request for high-risk subprocessors (subject to reasonable scoping and nondisclosure).

4) Audit rights: we can provide SOC2 reports and support an annual security attestation; on-site audits will be subject to standard confidentiality and scheduling terms — this is now reflected in the annex.

Attachments: Redwood_TOMs_Exhibit_v2.pdf (incorporates FinBank edits inline), Subprocessor_Inventory_2026-12-15.csv

If this aligns, we'll prepare the DocuSign envelope that locks the TOMs exhibit (Exhibit B) and the Security Annex so post-signature changes require mutual agreement.

--
Monica Patel
